newsitem.title: UK: Britain's ITV network determined to lead in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Britain's ITV network determined to lead in 1997.

text.p: Britain's Independent television (ITV) network is determined to maintain its leading position in 1997 and will spend about 800 million pounds ($1.24 billion) on programming, network director Marcus Plantin said on Monday.

"Next year ITV will be looking for much more consistency and better performance from our schedule," Plantin said at the launch of the 1997 programme schedule for advertisers and agencies, that will include more new drama, special events, sports and comedy.
"Last year out of 100 network shows, only three were deemed to be a hit," he said.
"In 1997 ITV has to set the pace," Plantin added. "ITV is unwavering in its determination to maintain its highest share of the ratings schedule."

The 1997 programming schedule is based on a six-point plan that includes more new drama, more special events, more comedy, continuing support of the network's home-grown soap operas, more sports and the re-introduction of U.S. movies and one-hour series.
ITV will spend about 300 million pounds on drama in 1997 and launch 23 new drama programmes, adding more than 90 hours of fresh drama to the schedule.
In outlining an expanded commitment to comedy, Plantin said it needs to be "...far more consistent and a vital part of the ITV schedule." There will be 10 new comedies in 1997.

Plantin acknowledged the ongoing concerns raised in the media on the influence on British culture by Hollywood, but he called movies a vital part of the schedule and emphasized that they continue to win high ratings.
U.S. movies to be shown on ITV in 1997 include "The Fugitive," "The Getaway," "Prince of Tides" and "Ace Ventura Pet Detective."

The proliferation of television channels has resulted in viewers wanting increased diversity and he said the decision to bring back American, one-hour series is part of the effort to meet that viewer demand.
ITV will also spend about 40 million pounds on children's programming in 1997, Plantin said.
ITV's 1997 programme schedule will be backed by a marketing campaign designed by M&C Saatchi.
